The grievance is structural: the F-35 expulsion of 2019, CAATSA sanctions of December 2020 and Washington's past support for the Syrian Kurds. The trend is warming under Trump: Erdogan was received at the White House on 25 Sep 2025 (and cut Russian crude after Trump's appeal), Trump said in Ankara on 7 Jul 2026 'we're going to be taking the sanctions off', Erdogan says he got 'a promise' on the F-35, and on 2 Oct Trump still gave no timetable. The legal barrier (congressionally mandated sanctions, the S-400 still in Turkey) is why this is a promise and not yet a change of structure. Bond - grievance.

stances_toward.note: Transactional, and it should not be read as an alliance: no treaty, direct US funding stopped in early 2025 (Kiel), the Trump administration asked the General Assembly on 24 Feb 2026 to drop the territorial-integrity paragraphs (69 to 11 against) and then abstained, and the Iran war froze the talks from March. Yet Washington remains the supplier Kyiv cannot replace (about 95% of Patriot interceptors reach Ukraine through PURL, paid by allies), the minerals fund has made its first deals, and the line changed in July 2026: at Ankara Trump promised a licence to build Patriot missiles and said he wants Ukrainian drones, then received Zelensky at the White House on 28 July. Trend: warming since July, with a Miami round on 9-10 Oct. Bond - none: pure interest after the US voted against Ukraine's resolution in Feb 2025.

relations_to.summary: Bucharest wants the US military presence kept and enlarged on its soil (Kogalniceanu, Deveselu) and a Dan-Trump meeting with an economic component; Dan said on 8 Jul 2026 he sees no risk of a pullback and discussed the Kogalniceanu expansion and US companies with a congressional delegation in Ankara.

relations_to.summary: About 1,000 US troops remain in Romania after the Pentagon decided (29 Oct 2025) not to replace the 2nd Brigade of the 101st Airborne; both Armed Services chairs opposed the decision. Kyiv Post's sources put the cut at a battalion, not a brigade.

relations_to.summary: Aegis Ashore Romania at Deveselu, a NATO ballistic-missile-defence site under US Naval Forces Europe-Africa control, with about 250 US personnel next to about 500 Romanian soldiers; reported operational and fully funded by the US Embassy. No 2025-26 change found.

relations_to.summary: Parliament approved the purchase of 32 F-35A fighters for an estimated USD 6.5bn, Romania's most expensive military buy; deliveries are expected in the early 2030s. One database lists 48; the signed-deal reporting says 32.

relations_to.summary: Within a day of the US request, the Supreme Council of National Defence and Parliament approved (11 Mar 2026) use of Mihail Kogalniceanu for refuelling aircraft, surveillance and satellite equipment in the US Iran operation (Epic Fury); Rutte later named Romania and Italy as participants and Iran accused NATO of complicity (June 2026).

relations_to.summary: Ankara wants F-35 readmission and the lifting of CAATSA sanctions (imposed Dec 2020 over the S-400): Trump said on 7 Jul 2026 in Ankara the sanctions would come off and called a sale 'something we would consider'; Erdogan says he got a promise and on 2 Sep 2026 that talks continue; on 2 Oct Trump gave no timetable. relations_to.summary: Trump and Erdogan met in Ankara on 7 Jul 2026 at the NATO summit, where Trump said 'we're going to be taking the sanctions off' and called an F-35 sale something the US would consider; the previous face-to-face was at the White House on 25 Sep 2025, where Trump urged an end to Russian oil purchases. Erdogan phoned Trump on 17 Aug 2026 to urge talks with Iran.
